subject: Urgent: LatentBridge inference latency & errors — RCA and follow-through
messages:
From: Samir Joshi <s.joshi@latentbridge.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: aisha.malik@latentbridge.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Increased latency & 500 errors on inference endpoints

Karthik / team,

We started seeing a sustained spike in p95/p99 latency and a growing 500 error rate on our production inference endpoints since ~08:45 PDT. Quick summary from our side: 
- p95 has moved from ~180ms -> ~1.1s; p99 up to ~2.8s
- 500 error rate peaked at ~8% for a 30m window
- Impact: user-facing request timeouts and retries; several customers reported failures

Attached: slo_violations.png (screenshot from our dashboard).

This is causing an active incident for us. We need an immediate triage and an ETA on a mitigation path. Can you confirm whether this is related to the recent runtime rollout / batching changes or if something else is hot?

When you reply, please include the bridge link/phone and let me know if we should fail traffic to smaller model variant.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Engineering, LatentBridge
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <s.joshi@latentbridge.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:30:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Increased latency & 500 errors on inference endpoints

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the data. We're bringing the incident bridge up now.

Immediate actions we are taking (first 30 minutes):
- Opened an incident bridge (link in internal only) and paging runtime team
- Rolling traffic to the compatible smaller model variant (canary) to reduce memory/KV pressure
- Increasing autoscaler buffers for the affected GPU pool to allow faster scale-up
- Collecting KV cache hit-rates and recent kernel selection logs (please send any request ids you have)

Can you share a short sample request-id or timestamp from your logs so we can correlate?

I will keep you posted on the bridge decisions and share an interim mitigation update in ~30–45m.

—Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:40:58 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Increased latency & 500 errors on inference endpoints

Samir / Karthik — quick status:
- Rolled traffic to the smaller variant at 09:33 PDT; early telemetry shows error rate dropping to ~1.2% but tail latency still elevated (p99 ~1.8s).
- We’ve disabled the recent batch-size auto-adjust on the affected pool to prevent spike from overshooting memory pressure; reverting the change if safe.
- Runtime team is instrumenting the KV cache eviction path and collecting per-instance GC/alloc metrics.

We’ll push a short-lived config that removes the experimental kernel selector fallback (this was part of last week's runtime tweak) if correlation looks strong. I’ll attach mitigation notes to the bridge notes after the call.

—Kimberly
Sr. Manager, Runtime Ops

Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 15:22:10 -07:00
Subject: Draft RCA & corrective actions — LatentBridge 2027-04-05 incident

Samir — attaching the initial RCA PDF and the correlated query logs for your team to review. Key points below and an action tracker appended.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: interaction between aggressive instant-batching heuristics and a kernel-selection regression introduced in runtime v2.14. The combination caused KV cache churn, memory pressure, and degraded kernel performance for a subset of mid-length sequences, producing elevated tail latency and transient 500s under load.
- Timeline:
  * 08:40 PDT — LatentBridge production traffic begins to show increased retry rates
  * 08:45 — first 500s observed; p95/p99 climb rapidly
  * 09:33 — traffic shifted to smaller model variant (mitigation)
  * 10:05 — error rate reduced to baseline; p99 still elevated into the afternoon

Corrective actions proposed (short + medium term):
- Short (0–48h):
  1) Revert the kernel-selection fallback introduced in v2.14 for affected families (rollback tag r2.14-hotfix).
  2) Temporarily tighten batching heuristics for high-throughput customers (config patch rolled at 09:58 PDT).
  3) Deploy a KV-cache metrics exporter and enable a high-severity alert for cache churn.
- Medium (1–3 weeks):
  1) Kernel performance regression fix (PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8124).
  2) Increase autoscaler responsiveness and validate cold-start latency under realistic traffic profiles.
  3) Add an automated canary check that runs the new kernel selector against a standard prompt corpus before rollout.

Attachments: latentbridge_rca_v1.pdf (detailed RCA, 12 pages), query_logs_20270405.csv (request ids + samples).

Planned next steps: final RCA review with LatentBridge on Apr 9 (exec readout). We will maintain an action tracker and deliverables matrix; the first version is attached as action_tracker_20270407.csv in the follow-up.

Please review and call out any items we missed. We will also include an itemized SLA credit proposal for your finance/procurement team in the exec readout.

—Grace
Principal Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Joshi <s.joshi@latentbridge.com>

Subject: Re: Draft RCA & corrective actions — LatentBridge 2027-04-05 incident

Grace / Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed RCA draft. A couple quick asks from LatentBridge: 
- Please include an explicit SLA credit calculation and the basis (minutes of downtime / error weight) for our procurement team.
- We need an exec-level readout (VP/CTO level) that summarizes customer impact and compensatory steps. Aisha (copied) will coordinate our side.

Otherwise the short/medium actions look reasonable. Can you confirm the expected ETA for the kernel PR landing in staging?

Samir
Head of Engineering, LatentBridge

Subject: LatentBridge — final actions, commitments, and exec readout scheduling

Samir / Aisha — following up with commitments and the next steps we discussed: 

What we are committing to today:
- Kernel PR (https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8124) targeted to land in staging by 2027-04-12 and production by 2027-04-19 following expanded canary validation.
- Autoscaler tuning and batching-heuristic adjustments deployed as hotfixes (completed 2027-04-06).
- KV-cache exporter and alerting deployed (active) with a new high-severity alert threshold.
- A post-incident action tracker attached (action_tracker_20270407.csv) with owners and target dates.
- Draft SLA credit calculation attached; we will finalize with finance in the exec readout.

Exec readout: Scheduled proposal — 2027-04-09 10:00 PDT (cal invite sent). Attendees: LatentBridge VP Eng, LatentBridge CTO (optionally), Redwood Head of Sales, Jonas Weber (VP Product), myself, Grace, Kimberly.

We understand the business impact and will provide a formal letter of incident summary and proposed credit. If you prefer a different readout time, let me know and we will accommodate.

Attachments: postmortem_slide_deck.pdf, action_tracker_20270407.csv, latentbridge_rca_v1.pdf (same as draft).

—Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
